transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-12-15 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Dr. Lena Ortega (Halcyon Head of Security), Marcus Liu (Halcyon Infra Lead), Priya Nair (Compliance)
---
Summary:
Quick posture orientation for SOC 2 / ISO 27001 readiness, walk through Trust Center access model, controls mapping expectations, and plan for KMS/integration proof points. Focus on evidence delivery paths and residency constraints.
Topics: trust center access, SOC2 Type II artifacts, ISO control mapping, RBAC & SSO (SAML), audit log retention, encryption (KMS/HSM), data residency, next steps and timeline.
---
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call and then we'll jump in. I see Lena, Marcus, Priya, and my colleague Ravi from infra. Hi all.
[00:10] Dr. Lena: hi thanks, yeah we wanted to make sure we had time today to understand how Redwood stores and presents evidence, and how that maps to our control matrix, primarily SOC2.
[00:20] Maya: totally, that's the goal. we'll do an orientation first, then show trust center nav, then address KMS and residency questions. quick note — audio may clip on my end, apologies.
[00:30] Marcus: no worries.
[00:35] Ravi: I'll jump in on the technical bits — encryption at rest, KMS integration patterns, and audit logging exports.
[00:40] Priya: great. and timeline wise, we're aiming to close our vendor assessment by end of January so any evidence we can review sooner the better.
[00:48] Maya: noted.
[02:12] Maya: first, high-level posture — Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II attestation and a mapped ISO 27001 Annex A reference. We publish the attestation bundle in the Trust Center with redactions allowed for sensitive bits. sometimes the scanner OCR shows typos in the auto extracts, so if something looks off, flag it and we'll get the source pdf.
[02:35] Dr. Lena: when you say "Trust Center" — is that a read-only console we can give to our auditors or do you export artifacts to our S3?
[02:45] Maya: both options. default is read-only Trust Center access with RBAC, you can create a read-only auditor role. we also can push zipped evidence to a customer-controlled S3 or SFTP on request for enterprise plans.
[03:05] Marcus: are there logs for every API call? we need three months of immutable logs for infra changes and admin events.
[03:12] Ravi: yes, we capture admin events, model rollout events, token usage and auth events. logs are stored in an append-only store for 90 days by default, retention can be extended. we can stream to your account via Kinesis/CloudWatch/S3 — choose whichever endpoint you prefer.
[03:30] Priya: retention policy is important for our compliance — do you do tamper-evidence or hash chains?
[03:37] Ravi: we provide signed log bundles (SHA256 manifests) and can integrate an optional write-once object lock in S3 for the exported artifacts. internal audit logs have integrity checks too.
[04:05] Dr. Lena: about encryption — do you manage keys or can we bring our own? we have policy to use customer-managed keys for production data.
[04:12] Maya: we support BYOK through external KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and HSM-backed keys for private deployments. Hosted customers can either use Redwood-managed keys or the BYOK route for the Dedicated/Private tiers.
[04:30] Marcus: curious about key rotation — is key rotation automated? what about re-keying for older stored artifacts?
[04:38] Ravi: rotation is supported; for BYOK we rely on customer's rotation policy. we support envelope encryption so data keys can be re-encrypted when you rotate the master key. older blobs can be re-wrapped — we have a migration tool but large backfills are something we'd plan with you.
[05:12] Maya: one common confusion — for Trust Center exports we redact PII/credentials by default, but we can produce un-redacted copies under an NDA or to a secure SFTP tied to an auditor.
[05:30] Dr. Lena: ok that helps. on the ISO mapping side, do you provide a controls matrix we can import into our GRC tool?
[05:38] Maya: yes, we maintain a controls mapping spreadsheet that maps SOC 2 controls and ISO Annex A to our internal policies and evidence artifacts. we'll share an annotated CSV that you can import.
[06:05] Priya: will that include control owner contacts and evidence filenames?
[06:09] Maya: it includes control IDs, evidence artifact names, location links (trust center or export path), and the responsible Redwood team contact (ops/security owner).
[07:00] [longer pause while Maya shares screen — transcript audio garble noted]
[07:30] Maya: switching to the Trust Center quick tour — link is trust-center.redwood.ai/halcyon (read-only). you'll see a Compliance > Reports page, an Evidence bucket, and a Controls Mapping tab.
[08:05] Marcus: I see the reports, but the nav labels are slightly off — my screen shows 'Reports (Beta)' — is that expected?
[08:12] Maya: yes, beta label — UI changes, sorry. the data behind it is stable though.
[09:20] [00:09:20] Ravi: on the audit logging export: when you enable streaming to your AWS account, we provision an IAM role with least privilege. events are delivered as newline-delimited JSON, with fields for event_type, user, timestamp, request_id, model_id, route, and metadata. small note — the transcript auto-cap called it kv-cache earlier, might show as 'k v cache' sometimes.
[10:00] Marcus: can we get an example log line to validate our SIEM parser?
[10:05] Ravi: yes — I'll attach a sample when I send the Kinesis schema.
[11:40] Dr. Lena: for the SOC2 Type II report, can we download the full report or only summary? our external auditors need the full attestation.
[11:48] Maya: full attestation is accessible as a PDF in Trust Center. we can grant a temporary auditor access token or do a one-time export to your S3 under restricted access.
[12:15] Priya: on evidence delivery cadence — if you produce weekly snapshot exports, is there a way to mark an artifact as 'final' for a given audit period?
[12:22] Ravi: yes we have audit snapshots capability — you can trigger an export snapshot, which stamps the set with a manifest and a hash. that becomes the canonical bundle for the period.
[13:05] Maya: quick question to Halcyon — what are your primary regions of operation? EU? APAC?
[13:12] Dr. Lena: primary is US and EU, some processing in Ireland and occasional customers in Singapore but not storing EU PII there. residency is: EU customer data must be in eu-west-1 or similar.
[13:30] Marcus: so we need EU-only storage for a subset of datasets and logs — can Redwood partition at tenant-level?
[13:36] Maya: yes, we support tenant-level region pinning for Dedicated and Private; hosted tier supports regional routing but full residency guarantees require Dedicated or Private.
[14:02] Dr. Lena: cost vs residency tradeoffs are expected. as long as we can certify for the audit.
[14:10] Maya: understood.
[15:00] [15:00] Ravi: on SSO — Redwood supports SAML 2.0 SSO and OIDC for provisioning. we support SCIM for user provisioning and can configure role-based mappings from your IdP to Redwood RBAC roles.
[15:18] Dr. Lena: we'd like to map our IdP groups to auditor/read-only and infra-admin roles — can that be done per-team?
[15:25] Ravi: yes, per-organization or per-team mappings. we apply least-privilege by default and you can request additional roles.
[16:05] Priya: can we get a sample SAML assertion or mapping doc?
[16:09] Ravi: I'll attach the SSO mapping doc in the follow-up.
[17:10] Dr. Lena: one more around service accounts — do you have service principal rotation and key lifecycle docs? we need to show evidence that service accounts are rotated and that secrets are not long-lived.
[17:20] Maya: we have an internal service account policy, rotation every 90 days by default, and ephemeral tokens where possible. evidence for rotation is in the change log and the credential issuance audit.
[18:00] Marcus: about private deployment — if we went with Private, could we bring a customer KMS and an HSM appliance?
[18:08] Ravi: yes for on-prem/private we can integrate with customer HSMs using PKCS#11 or KMIP depending on the appliance. HSM-backed attestation available for enterprise plans.
[18:40] [crosstalk, a bit of overlap]
[19:00] Dr. Lena: regarding the control mappings — can we get the ISO Annex A references? our auditor wants ISO IDs (A.5, A.6 etc) in the mapping.
[19:07] Maya: absolutely — the mapping includes ISO Annex A IDs. some items map to multiple SOC2 criteria, so we include those crosswalks.
[20:05] Priya: evidence naming convention is important — would you accept our naming scheme? we want the artifact name to include environment, date, and control ID.
[20:13] Ravi: yes we can append a metadata tag to artifacts to include your naming scheme; exported archives maintain that metadata.
[21:40] Maya: ok next — procurement questions: is Redwood willing to sign a tailored DPA and specific data residency addendum?
[21:48] Maya: short answer yes, for Dedicated/Private we include residency addenda; for hosted we'll discuss addendum clauses. legal typically takes 2-3 weeks to iterate.
[22:30] Dr. Lena: what about subprocessor lists and notification timelines?
[22:36] Maya: we publish subprocessors in the Trust Center and we provide 30 days' notice for major changes, and immediate notice for security incidents per the SLA.
[23:05] Marcus: SLA levels — do you offer uptime and latency SLOs for Dedicated?
[23:10] Maya: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets, we'll share the SLA doc.
[24:06] [longer technical detour — Ravi explains envelope encryption diagram — some audio gaps]
[27:10] Ravi: diagrammatically: customer master key in KMS encrypts a data key, data key encrypts objects. we never store plaintext master keys. rotation: re-wrap the data key with the new master. for audit we provide key usage logs (who called KMS:Encrypt/Decrypt).
[28:00] Dr. Lena: can we have those KMS logs forwarded to our security account?
[28:04] Ravi: yes, that's part of the integration plan — we'll stream to your logging account.
[29:40] Priya: for the SOC2 evidence — are change management tickets linked to artifacts? we need traceability from control to ticket to evidence.
[29:48] Maya: we link deployments, change requests (Jira ticket IDs), and the generated artifact. the control mapping CSV includes ticket references where applicable.
[31:00] Marcus: regulatory question — do you support data residency certification for EU data under SCCs?
[31:06] Maya: we can sign Data Processing Agreements incorporating SCCs; for strict residency we recommend Dedicated/Private.
[32:15] Dr. Lena: about penetration tests and frequency — do you perform third-party pen tests and can we review the summary?
[32:22] Maya: yes, annual third-party pen tests and we publish an executive summary in Trust Center. full reports are under NDA.
[33:40] Priya: what about background checks for staff with access to production?
[33:45] Maya: Redwood does role-based background checks for employees with access to production secrets; details are in our HR security policy in the Trust Center.
[34:50] [short pause, someone returns to the room]
[36:10] Dr. Lena: can you outline the timeline for evidence handoff if we decide to pilot?
[36:18] Maya: timeline example: Week 0 — sign NDA/trust access; Week 1 — grant read-only trust center + sample exports; Week 2 — provide SOC2 bundle and controls mapping; Week 3 — technical deep dive for KMS and SSO; Weeks 4–6 — pilot evidence collection and final audit snapshot.
[36:45] Marcus: that aligns with our Jan audit window if we start now.
[37:05] Maya: Great.
[38:50] Ravi: quick note — for secure artifact delivery we prefer S3 cross-account or SFTP with IP allowlist; we can also support ephemeral signed URLs for auditors.
[39:20] Dr. Lena: last question: how do you handle data deletion requests and proof of deletion?
[39:28] Maya: we support deletion APIs with purge workflows; for proof we provide deletion manifests and retention policy logs showing lifecycle transitions.
[40:15] Priya: will those manifests be included in the evidence bundles?
[40:20] Maya: yes, included as retention/deletion evidence.
[41:00] [small technical back-and-forth about export throttling limits and packaging]
[43:10] Marcus: any blockers we should be aware of?
[43:14] Maya: only if you require full EU residency on hosted tier — that's a blocker; otherwise we can provision everything else.
[44:05] Dr. Lena: good to know.
[45:00] [wrap-up] Maya: to recap — Redwood will share the annotated SOC2 PDF and controls mapping CSV, Ravi will attach KMS/SSO docs and a log sample, Halcyon will confirm residency sub-scope. we'll target the technical deep dive the week of 12/22.
[45:30] Dr. Lena: that works. thanks, appreciate the clarity.
[45:40] Priya: thanks everyone.
[46:00] Maya: I'll follow up with links and timeline notes.
[46:05] Marcus: thanks.
